report.title: Four coffee shops, one year: what sells and where
report.summary: Sandwiches are your best seller by a distance: one sale in five, but 32% of the money, because at $8.90 they cost far more than anything else on the menu. Downtown is your busiest shop, with $124,277 over the year, 1.74 times Midtown. Weekends are 15% busier than weekdays. Discounts sell a few more items but bring in almost no extra money, and customers who got one rated their visit a little lower. Sales held steady through the year, and the best month was the last: December, at $37,007.

insights.title: Sandwiches bring in a third of the money
insights.body: One sale in five is a sandwich, yet sandwiches took $122,041 of the $381,667 the shops made this year. It is not that more of them sell: every product sells about 31 a day at each shop. A sandwich simply costs $8.90, nearly three times a drip coffee at $3.10.

chart.label: Sales by product, 2025
chart.desc: Total revenue from each product over the year.

insights.title: Downtown is your busiest shop
insights.body: Downtown took $124,277 this year, a third of everything, against $71,244 at Midtown. The gap comes from how much people buy, not what they pay: prices are the same in every shop, but Downtown sells about 41 of a product on a typical day and Midtown about 22. Whatever brings people into Downtown is worth copying.

chart.label: Sales by shop, 2025
chart.desc: Total revenue at each of the four shops over the year.

insights.title: Weekends are 15% busier
insights.body: On an average Saturday or Sunday the four shops take in $1,155; on a weekday, $1,002. Sunday is the best day of the week and Friday the quietest. Weekend staff and stock deserve the most attention.

chart.label: Sales on an average day
chart.desc: Average revenue a day across the four shops, for each day of the week.

insights.title: Discounts sell more items, not more money
insights.body: Four sales in five had no discount. When there was one, about 35 items sold instead of 30, but the money barely moved: $168 a row against $162, a gap too small to rely on. Customers who got a discount also rated their visit a little lower, 4.17 out of 5 against 4.30. On these numbers, discounts are not bringing in extra money.

chart.label: Items sold, with and without a discount
chart.desc: Average items sold a row, for sales with a discount and without one.

insights.title: A steady year with a strong finish
insights.body: Monthly sales stayed between $26,295 in June and $37,007 in December. The second half of the year brought in 7% more than the first, but sales go up and down so much from week to week that this is not yet a trend to plan around.

chart.label: Sales by month, 2025
chart.desc: Total revenue across the four shops in each month.

report.conclusion: Your money comes from sandwiches and from Downtown, and weekends matter more than weekdays. Three things are worth trying: keep sandwiches stocked and easy to see in every shop, above all at weekends; find out what brings people into Downtown and try it at Midtown; and use discounts sparingly, since they move items but not money. Check again with next year's figures to see whether the strong finish to 2025 holds.

answers.q: Which store made the most revenue, and how much was it?
answers.a: Downtown store made the most revenue, with a total of $124,276.64.

answers.q: Did discounts make customers less satisfied?
answers.a: A little. Customers who got a discount rated their visit 4.17 out of 5 on average, against 4.30 for those who didn't. The gap is small, and it doesn't show that the discount caused it.

answers.q: Which product brought in the most revenue?
answers.a: The Sandwich product generated the most revenue, with a total of $122,040.59 across all transactions.

answers.q: What was the total revenue for the whole period?
answers.a: The total revenue for the entire period is $381,667.10.
